title: OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap Leaves After Eight Years to Launch New Venture
excerpt: The longtime executive's departure is the latest in a string of high-profile exits from the ChatGPT maker as it prepares for an initial public offering.
body:
• Brad Lightcap, who joined OpenAI in 2018 and served as COO since 2022, is leaving the company to start a new venture.
  • Lightcap had already transitioned to a "special projects" role in April, with Denise Dresser absorbing his operational duties.
  • His departure follows CEO of AGI deployment Fidji Simo's step-down in July and comes amid a broader wave of executive moves across AI labs.
  • OpenAI is preparing for an initial public offering after raising $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation earlier this year.

Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI's longest-serving executives, announced Tuesday that he is leaving the artificial intelligence company to pursue a new venture, marking the latest high-profile departure from the ChatGPT maker as it gears up for a blockbuster initial public offering.

"It is bittersweet to share that I'll be moving on from OpenAI to start something new," Lightcap wrote in a message to staff that he subsequently posted on X. "I feel incredibly fortunate to have spent most of the last decade pursuing our mission and building this company. Sitting here today, mission success feels within sight."

A Quiet Transition Months in the Making

Lightcap's exit did not come as a surprise to those tracking OpenAI's leadership. In April, he stepped away from the chief operating officer role he had held since 2022, moving to a newly created position overseeing "special projects" — including complex deals and the company's push to sell enterprise software through a joint venture with private equity firms. He reported directly to CEO Sam Altman in that capacity.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=yi1I4DNZZNk

Denise Dresser, the former Slack CEO who joined OpenAI as chief revenue officer, absorbed most of Lightcap's operational responsibilities. A source close to the company told Barron's that OpenAI does not expect his departure to affect day-to-day operations, given that the transition was effectively completed months ago.

"Over the last few months, I've been focused on the next horizon and what would stand in the way of mission success. I believe there are a few important new things the world will need to get right as we enter this next period."

— Brad Lightcap, in his X post announcing the departure

Executive Exodus Across AI Labs

Lightcap's departure extends a pattern of senior exits that has reshaped OpenAI's leadership bench at a critical moment. In July, Fidji Simo, who held the title of CEO of AGI deployment and oversaw much of the company's core business, stepped down from her full-time role to become a part-time adviser. Simo had been on medical leave since April for a neuroimmune condition. Chief marketing officer Kate Rouch also left her position earlier this year to focus on cancer recovery.

The churn is not confined to OpenAI. Across the AI industry, high-profile researchers and executives are on the move. Alphabet AI veteran Jeff Dean left the company last week to found a startup, while Nobel Prize winner Demis Hassabis stepped back from his role as CEO of Google's DeepMind lab. AI researchers Noam Shazeer and John Jumper recently swapped Google for OpenAI and Anthropic, respectively. The movements signal a fierce talent war as AI labs compete for the small pool of researchers capable of pushing the frontier.

IPO Preparations in Focus

The leadership changes come as OpenAI prepares for what is expected to be one of the largest technology IPOs in years. The company announced plans to go public in early June, following a $122 billion funding round in March that valued it at $852 billion. Investors will be watching closely to ensure the company has a stable executive team in place as it approaches an IPO roadshow.

Lightcap's tenure predates much of OpenAI's commercial success. He joined in 2018 — years before ChatGPT's launch turned the company into a household name — after previously working with Altman at venture capital firm Y Combinator. During his time as COO, he helped scale the company from a research lab into a commercial operation with nearly 1 billion users and rapidly growing enterprise revenue.

While Lightcap has not disclosed details of his next venture, his parting note struck a conciliatory tone: "I'll have more to share soon, but I believe in OpenAI more than ever and am excited to help you all advance the mission from a different vantage point."
